items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer asks if Marian McPartland's husband (Jimmy McPartland) heard Fats Navarro, and Marian responds about Jimmy's feelings. Marian herself does not describe a personal interaction with Fats Navarro.

ctx.x: I’ve got it, but I would . . . soon as I find it, I’ll dub it off for you.

I mentioned about some of the others. How did he feel about, and I just want to get a little bit of insight, because I know he was a very important influence on you as well, so this may eventually, this will tie in to what we’re saying, how is his feeling about swing music and about bebop or even more, say, more contemporary, like I say, did he hear Fats Navarro? Did he have any comments about Clifford Brown or Lee Morgan or some of the players that came up 20 years, 30 years after his time?

Yeah, but he was . . . he admitted that he was . . . he felt that he was committed to the style that he played. I think a lot of the . . . even sometimes with Dizzy, he would say, “It seems that all they do is play a lot of notes.” And yet when anybody would play a beautiful ballad or something, he would always dig that. I couldn’t hear him . . . he didn’t . . . I couldn’t see him getting into bebop. I think he had the style of playing so set in his mind that he wasn’t or couldn’t or wouldn’t change it. But at…
